$comment: The judgement calls — everything that cannot be extracted from code. Props, tokens, tests and adoption are generated; this file holds what a human decided.
summary: Renders any SVG icon component at a system size, decorative by default.
description: Icon wraps an SVG icon component — lucide-react is the recommended source, but anything that renders an <svg> and accepts SVG props works. It owns the two things every call site otherwise gets wrong: sizing (an em-based scale that tracks the surrounding text) and semantics (aria-hidden unless a label makes it meaningful). Colour is inherited from the text via the icon set's own currentColor.
useFor: Reinforcing adjacent text: a save icon next to 'Save changes'
Meaning-carrying glyphs with a `label`: a status dot in a table cell with no text
Consistent sizing of mixed icon sources so they line up on one row
dontUseFor: Icon-only actions — use Button with a required aria-label; an Icon is not interactive and has no focus or hit-target handling
Illustrations and logos — those are images with fixed art direction; use with alt text
Loading state — use the component's own `loading` prop (Button, etc.), which also announces via aria-busy

provides: aria-hidden by default, so purely decorative icons are silent instead of announced as 'image'
role="img" + aria-label set together by the `label` prop, so a meaningful icon is always named
The broken states are unrepresentable: aria-hidden, aria-label and role are removed from the prop types, so a role with no name or a name on a hidden node cannot compile
focusable="false", so legacy engines never put the svg in the tab order
consumerMustProvide: A `label` whenever the icon is the only carrier of meaning — decorative-by-default means an unlabelled status icon says nothing to a screen reader
Labels that name the MEANING ('Delivery failed'), not the glyph ('red triangle')
limitations: Icon renders one glyph; it does not manage tooltips. A meaning-carrying icon usually needs a visible affordance for sighted users too — `label` fixes the screen reader, not the squint.

doDont.do: Let a decorative icon stay silent: <Icon icon={Check} /> next to the text 'Saved'
doDont.dont: Label an icon whose meaning the adjacent text already states
doDont.why: A labelled icon beside equivalent text makes screen readers announce everything twice — 'Saved, Saved'. Decorative is the correct default, which is why it IS the default.

doDont.do: Name the meaning when the icon stands alone: <Icon icon={AlertTriangle} label="Delivery failed" />
doDont.dont: Ship a bare <Icon icon={AlertTriangle} /> as the only failure indicator in a table cell
doDont.why: aria-hidden by default means an unlabelled icon does not exist to assistive tech. A sighted user sees a warning; a screen reader user hears an empty cell.

doDont.do: Import icons at the call site: import { Truck } from 'lucide-react'
doDont.dont: Re-export the icon set (or an icons/index.ts barrel) from the design system
doDont.why: Icons are the classic bundle blowout: one barrel re-export can drag a four-digit count of components past tree-shaking. Consumers importing directly pay only for the icons they use.

doDont.do: Make icon-only actions a Button: <Button variant="ghost" aria-label="Dismiss"><Icon icon={X} /></Button>
doDont.why: An Icon is presentation only — no focus, no keyboard activation, no 44px hit target, no role. A clickable icon works for exactly one input method: a mouse, aimed well.

examples.title: Decorative (the default)
examples.description: Adjacent text carries the meaning, so the icon is aria-hidden and inherits the text colour automatically.

examples.title: Meaningful
examples.description: The icon is the only content, so `label` names it — role="img" and aria-label are set together.
examples.code:
import { AlertTriangle } from 'lucide-react';

<Icon icon={AlertTriangle} label="Delivery failed" />

examples.title: Sizes
examples.description: Em-based: `md` is 20px inside body text and scales with whatever type size surrounds it.
examples.code:
<Icon icon={Truck} size="sm" />
<Icon icon={Truck} size="md" />
<Icon icon={Truck} size="lg" />

examples.title: Inside a Button
examples.description: The Button owns the semantics; the icon stays decorative.
